tests: Polygon Art; rhyming text; two animal characters with distinctive clothing (bobble hat and scarf vs waistcoat and wellies) that must not swap
title: Pickle and Sock's Picnic Rhyme
subtitle: A bouncy tale of two best friends
user_prompt: A penguin called Pickle and a fox cub called Sock plan a picnic on a hill, but the wind keeps blowing their things away. Written in rhyme.
synopsis: Pickle the penguin and Sock the fox cub pack a picnic and climb Blossom Hill. A cheeky wind steals the blanket, the sandwiches and Pickle's hat, and the friends chase each item down the hill. They learn that the best picnic spot is the sheltered one, and share the last sandwich.

characters.name: Pickle
characters.physical_description: A small, round penguin with glossy black and white feathers, a short orange beak and orange feet. Always wears a yellow knitted bobble hat and a red scarf.

characters.name: Sock
characters.physical_description: A lively fox cub with bright orange fur, a white chest and a bushy tail with a white tip. Wears a green waistcoat with three brass buttons and blue wellies.

hair_attributes.colour: bright orange fur with a white-tipped tail

clothing_attributes.top: green waistcoat with three brass buttons

pages.text: Pickle the penguin, in her yellow bobble hat, packed a picnic basket, round and fat.
Sock the fox cub buttoned his green waistcoat tight, and pulled on his wellies, blue and bright.
Up Blossom Hill the two friends went, with sandwiches, apples and a lemony scent.
They spread their blanket at the very top. Then WHOOSH went the wind, and it didn't stop!
The blanket flapped and flew away. 'Come back!' cried Sock. 'We want to stay!'
Pickle waddled fast, Sock ran with a bound, and they caught the blanket on the soft green ground.
Then the wind gave a giggle and a mischievous puff, and off flew the sandwiches, crusts and stuff!
Sock leapt high and caught one in the air. Pickle slid on her tummy to catch one there.
Then off went Pickle's bobble hat, spinning past a very surprised black cat.
It landed in a hedge behind a big oak tree, where the air was still and calm as could be.
'This is the spot!' said Sock with a grin. So they set out their picnic where no wind could get in.
They shared the last sandwich, half and half, and the wind joined in with a whistling laugh.

tests: Polygon Art; educational theme; one child character with glasses and a raincoat; two pages need short, correctly spelled in-scene text (LIBRARY sign, SCIENCE FAIR banner)
title: Ada and the Library of Lights
subtitle: How a rainbow is made
user_prompt: Ada wants to win the school science fair. At the library she learns how sunlight and raindrops make rainbows, and builds her own with a glass of water.
synopsis: On a rainy day Ada visits the town library to find an idea for the science fair. A book shows her that sunlight is made of many colours and that raindrops bend it into a rainbow. She tries it at home with a glass of water and a torch, then shows her rainbow at the SCIENCE FAIR.

characters.name: Ada
characters.physical_description: A curious seven-year-old girl with brown skin and black hair in two high puffs tied with yellow bobbles. She wears round red glasses, a purple raincoat over a striped t-shirt, and white trainers.

hair_attributes.style: two high puffs with yellow bobbles

clothing_attributes.top: purple raincoat over a red and white striped t-shirt

pages.text: Rain tapped on the window. Ada pressed her nose to the glass. 'I need an idea for the science fair,' she said.
She zipped up her purple raincoat and splashed down the street to a tall building with a big sign that read LIBRARY.
Inside, the shelves went up and up. Ada pushed her red glasses up her nose and began to look.
She found a book with a rainbow on the cover and sat on a beanbag to read it.
The book said that sunlight looks white, but it is really made of many colours mixed together.
When sunlight shines through a raindrop, the drop bends the light and splits it into red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet.
'So every rainbow is made of millions of tiny raindrops,' Ada whispered. 'I want to make one!'
At home, Ada filled a glass with water and set it on the windowsill. She shone a torch through it.
Nothing happened. Ada tilted the glass a little, then a little more.
Suddenly a small rainbow appeared on the white wall. Ada clapped her hands.
On Friday she carried her glass, her torch and a poster to the school hall, under a banner that said SCIENCE FAIR.
Everyone gathered round as Ada made her rainbow. 'Light is full of colours,' she said, 'you just have to bend it!'

tests: Anime; four characters including identical twins who differ only by colour (red vs blue ribbon and hoodie): the strongest attribute-bleed test; an older man with a stick
title: The Twins and the Great Kite Race
subtitle: Red, blue and a very windy day
user_prompt: Twin sisters Mae and June race their kites against their friend Oscar at the park, with Grandad Ken as the judge. Mae's kite is red and June's is blue.
synopsis: Identical twins Mae and June, their friend Oscar and Grandad Ken go to Windy Hill Park for the great kite race. Mae flies a red kite and June a blue one. When Oscar's kite gets stuck in a tree, the twins stop racing to help him, and Grandad Ken declares all three the winners.

characters.name: Mae
characters.physical_description: An eight-year-old girl, identical twin to June, with straight black shoulder-length hair tied with a RED ribbon. She wears a RED hoodie, denim shorts and white trainers.

hair_attributes.style: straight, tied with a red ribbon

characters.name: June
characters.physical_description: An eight-year-old girl, identical twin to Mae, with straight black shoulder-length hair tied with a BLUE ribbon. She wears a BLUE hoodie, denim shorts and white trainers.

hair_attributes.style: straight, tied with a blue ribbon

characters.name: Oscar
characters.physical_description: A nine-year-old boy with curly brown hair, freckles and a gap-toothed grin. He wears a green cap, an orange t-shirt and grey shorts.

characters.name: Grandad Ken
characters.physical_description: A cheerful seventy-year-old man with a short grey beard, wearing a flat cap, a tan cardigan and brown trousers, and walking with a wooden stick.

hair_attributes.style: short with a short grey beard

clothing_attributes.accessories: wooden walking stick and a whistle

pages.text: It was the windiest day of the year. Mae tied her red ribbon and June tied her blue one. 'Race day!' they shouted together.
Grandad Ken led the way to Windy Hill Park, tapping his wooden stick and swinging a silver whistle.
Their friend Oscar was already waiting at the top, holding a yellow diamond kite and grinning his gap-toothed grin.
Mae unrolled her red kite. June unrolled her blue kite. Oscar checked his string twice.
Grandad Ken raised his whistle. 'Ready... steady... FLY!' The whistle blew.
The three kites leapt into the sky: red, blue and yellow, dancing over the hill.
Mae's red kite swooped left. June's blue kite looped right. The twins laughed as their strings crossed and uncrossed.
Then a gust caught Oscar's yellow kite and tangled it high in the branches of an old oak tree.
Oscar's face fell. Mae and June looked at each other, then reeled their kites back down.
June held Mae steady while Mae climbed onto Grandad Ken's shoulders and gently unhooked the yellow kite.
Oscar hugged his kite. 'You gave up the race for me!' he said.
Grandad Ken blew his whistle one last time. 'The winners are Mae, June and Oscar,' he declared, 'for being the best team on the hill!'
